findings.description: The new file-level `vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 30_000 })` (line 29) makes the per-test `}, 30_000);` overrides at lines 726, 742, 769, 803, 852, 1403 and 1416 redundant, because they set the same value. The two `}, 20_000);` overrides at 1447 and 2687 now shorten the timeout below the 30 s file default, which is probably unintended. Drop the seven redundant overrides and decide deliberately about the two 20_000 ones.

Other test files set timeouts with the suite-scoped `describe('...', { timeout: N }, ...)` form (code-map.test.ts:42, review.test.ts:75, fix-round.test.ts:162). This file is the only one using the global `vi.setConfig`. That is defensible because the file has several top-level describes, but it departs from the established pattern.

The WHY comment is accurate: a timeout fails the instrumented vitest run, so `pup audit` reports coverage as unavailable. The phrase 'times out a different one each run' is flaky-test narration that will go stale. A tighter wording would be: "Many tests spawn real git and sh and exceed the 5 s default under load or coverage; a timeout fails the instrumented run, so `pup audit` reports coverage as not measured."

process_issues.description: Every Bash call (orchestrator and subagents) failed with `apply-seccomp: write /proc/self/setgroups (nested userns is capability-restricted; caller must provide CAP_SYS_ADMIN): Permission denied`. The review could not read `gh pr view`, `gh pr diff`, `git diff <merge_base>..HEAD`, or `git log -L`. Reviewers inspected only the HEAD state of src/core/profile-compiler.test.ts (located via Grep), so provenance of the per-test 30_000 overrides could not be established. The §2 second freshness assertion (HEAD vs headRefOid) could not be performed. PR title/body, steering threads and closing-issue references could not be read.

Because the diff was unreadable, gating relied on the latest commit message (5b54cfe, test-only timeout change) and Grep. Only conventions and docs were spawned; correctness, security, maintainability, context and spec were skipped as untouched/no spec source found, but this could not be confirmed against the actual file list.
